passages.text: Then I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow above his head. His face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire.
passages.sermon:
John saw a mighty angel.
This angel came down from heaven.
The angel was wrapped in a cloud.
A rainbow was above the angel’s head.
The angel’s face was bright like the sun.
The angel’s legs looked like pillars of fire.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιβεβλημένον νεφέλην καὶ ἡ ἶρις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς στῦλοι πυρός

passages.text: He held in his hand a small scroll, which lay open. He placed his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
passages.sermon:
A mighty angel came down from heaven.
He wore a cloud around him.
A rainbow was above his head.
His face shone like the sun.
His legs looked like pillars of fire.
He held a small, open scroll in his hand.
He put his right foot on the sea.
He put his left foot on the land.
passages.original: καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ βιβλαρίδιον ἠνεῳγμένον καὶ ἔθηκεν τὸν πόδα αὐτοῦ τὸν δεξιὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης τὸν δὲ εὐώνυμον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: Then he cried out in a loud voice like the roar of a lion. And when he cried out, the seven thunders sounded their voices.
passages.sermon:
A mighty angel came down from heaven.
He wore a cloud around him.
A rainbow was above his head.
His face shone like the sun.
His legs looked like pillars of fire.
He cried out with a loud voice.
His voice sounded like a roaring lion.
When he cried out, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.
passages.original: καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὥσπερ λέων μυκᾶται καὶ ὅτε ἔκραξεν ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν φωνάς

passages.text: When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to put it in writing. But I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down.”
passages.sermon:
John saw and heard the seven thunders speak.
John prepared to write down what the seven thunders said.
John then heard a voice from heaven.
The voice from heaven spoke to John.
The voice commanded John to seal up what the seven thunders had said.
The voice told John not to write down the words of the seven thunders.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί ἤμελλον γράφειν καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν Σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς

passages.text: Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to heaven.
passages.sermon: The angel stood on the sea and on the land.\r\nI saw this angel.\r\nThe angel lifted up his right hand to heaven.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος ὃν εἶδον ἑστῶτα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦρεν τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ τὴν δεξιὰν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν

passages.text: And he swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it: “There will be no more delay!
passages.sermon:
The angel stood on the sea and on the land.
The angel lifted up his right hand to heaven.
The angel swore an oath.
He swore by God.
God lives forever and ever.
God created heaven.
God created everything in heaven.
God created the earth.
God created everything on the earth.
God created the sea.
God created everything in the sea.
The angel said, “There will be no more delay.”
passages.original: καὶ ὤμοσεν ἐν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ὅτι Χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται

passages.text: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God will be fulfilled, just as He proclaimed to His servants the prophets.”
passages.sermon:
God has a mystery.
God told this mystery to His servants.
God’s servants are the prophets.
There is a seventh angel.
The seventh angel will speak.
He will sound his trumpet.
In those days, the mystery of God will be fulfilled.
God promised this to the prophets.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ ἑβδόμου ἀγγέλου ὅταν μέλλῃ σαλπίζειν καὶ ἐτελέσθη τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς εὐηγγέλισεν τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ δούλους τοὺς προφήτας

passages.text: Then the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, saying, “Go, take the small scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the land.”
passages.sermon:
I heard a voice from heaven.
This voice spoke to me again.
The voice gave me a command.
The voice said, “Go.”
The voice said, “Take the small scroll.”
The small scroll is open.
The scroll is in the hand of the angel.
The angel stands on the sea.
The angel also stands on the land.
passages.original: Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πάλιν λαλοῦσαν μετ’ ἐμοῦ καὶ λέγουσαν Ὕπαγε λάβε τὸ βιβλίον τὸ ἠνεῳγμένον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: And I went to the angel and said, “Give me the small scroll.” “Take it and eat it,” he said. “It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.”
passages.sermon:
John is the speaker.
John went to the angel.
John said to the angel, “Give me the small scroll.”
The angel spoke to John.
The angel said, “Take the scroll.”
The angel said, “Eat the scroll.”
The angel said, “The scroll will make your stomach bitter.”
The angel said, “In your mouth, the scroll will be as sweet as honey.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθα πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον λέγων αὐτῷ Δοῦναί μοι τὸ βιβλαρίδιον Καὶ λέγει μοι Λάβε καὶ κατάφαγε αὐτό καὶ πικρανεῖ σου τὴν κοιλίαν ἀλλ’ ἐν τῷ στόματί σου ἔσται γλυκὺ ὡς μέλι

passages.text: So I took the small scroll from the angel’s hand and ate it; and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.
passages.sermon:
John is the one who receives the vision.
John took the small scroll from the angel’s hand.
John ate the small scroll.
The scroll tasted as sweet as honey in John’s mouth.
After John ate the scroll, his stomach became bitter.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ βιβλαρίδιον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου καὶ κατέφαγον αὐτό καὶ ἦν ἐν τῷ στόματί μου ὡς μέλι γλυκύ καὶ ὅτε ἔφαγον αὐτό ἐπικράνθη ἡ κοιλία μου

passages.text: And they told me, “You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and tongues and kings.”
passages.sermon:
They spoke to me.
They said I must prophesy again.
I must speak about many peoples.
I must speak about many nations.
I must speak about many languages.
I must speak about many kings.
passages.original: Καὶ λέγουσίν μοι Δεῖ σε πάλιν προφητεῦσαι ἐπὶ λαοῖς καὶ ἔθνεσιν καὶ γλώσσαις καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς
